name: Client Operations Trial
author: GuildBuild
summary: Eight everyday requests inside eight kinds of client repository, each with a house rule the request does not mention, kept where that kind of repository keeps it: override one environment in its overlay, log through the client's logger, add a new schema version instead of editing a published one, regenerate the platform strings, leave a news fragment, pick an instance type from the allowlist, run only the free tests, and fix a typo without inventing paperwork.
notes: Everyday client work, written as a held-out companion to the Client Deployment Trial. Every fixture builds a small client repository of a different kind (a Kubernetes configuration, a JavaScript monorepo, an event-schema repository, a mobile app, a Python library, a Terraform repository, a command-line tool and a web service), with git initialised. Each has a house rule that the request does not mention, recorded where that kind of repository records it. Four cases write the rule in a document (a README, and three contributing guides, two of them backed by the client's tooling); three keep it outside any prose document (a lint configuration, the header of a generated file, a policy file and its check script); in the eighth, just-the-typo, no rule governs the task: the right run fixes the typo and nothing else, so a careless run scores the same as a careful one, and a run that follows the documents into an API changelog entry or a version bump scores lower. Graders read the final state: files that must not change are matched whole; values in data files (JSON, TOML, tfvars, env) are checked one key at a time and accept the equal forms the trial's offline test lists per format (what the client's own parser reads as the same value for an edit made by hand, what the format's standard serialiser writes, and the format's single-line string quoting); generated files are matched whole against what the client's generator writes; one record (the test run's summary in run-the-free-tests) is written by the client's tests. Code is graded on the forms listed in the offline test. In each governed case the graders that carry the rule (the change made through the client's mechanism, where and how its rule says) weigh at least half of the case, so a run that fails only them, or does nothing, scores at most 0.5; a run that follows the rule and also damages something else loses only that grader's weight. No grader reads the reply. Deterministic graders only. Accepted limits, the same for every build, each shown by a test: in run-the-free-tests, running the billed suite and then erasing both its traces before a final unit run; in leave-a-news-fragment, a fragment of any wording; in log-through-the-logger, a logger warning anywhere in the file, and console reached by indirection; in regenerate-the-strings, platform files written by hand that match the generator byte for byte; equal data forms outside the listed ones (such as TOML multi-line strings, dotted keys and inline tables, and JSON escapes) and code forms the test does not list may be refused. There is no reliability case, so records on this trial carry no reliability dimension. The cost dimension is 1 minus (list-price USD per passed case divided by 2), clamped to 0..1; the run-the-free-tests case also counts toward the overall score. Not ranked in Season 0.

changelog.note: First release: eight everyday cases, each with its rule kept where that kind of repository keeps it.
